With regard to his comment: **“As I know that he will enter no other academy,”** that serves to exclude **the academies of Hezekiah, king of Judah and Ahijah the Shilonite** (section 58).

[The Zohar ] continues: **“The Messiah shuddered and raised his voice** etc.” On account of the revelation of the end, which Metatron revealed – that at the time there will be terrible troubles for Israel, the firmaments will shake, and so will the Great Sea, and the world will overturn, in the mystical meaning of “(the world will) lie in ruins for one (thousand years”; Sanhedrin 97a) – he therefore raised his voice, as he wanted to temper all these shocks.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“Who admitted here a man dressed in a garment of that world?”** The Messiah was surprised by Rabbi Ḥiyya, who was dressed in the corporeal body of this world – **“in a garment of that world.”** Since he merited to be here and merited the revelation of Metatron and his oath, he has thus already rectified all the evil aspects [within himself] (as stated in section 56 above, second to last paragraph; see there), and has likewise merited receiving the Messiah. Accordingly, he has completed all his work in this world and has nothing more to do in this world. Consequently, he should depart and enter the academy of Rabbi Shimon in the Garden of Eden. Why, then, should he remain in this world for no reason?

[The Zohar ] concludes: **“Rabbi Shimon said, let time be given to him.”** In other words, Rabbi Shimon proved to him that (Rabbi Ḥiyya) should be given fresh time, since he still needs to live in this world and engage in new rectifications. Subsequently, **“they gave him time,”** that is, the Messiah and Rabbi Shimon informed him of what he still has to do in this world.

**60. “And he departed from there shocked etc.” And** the Messiah **departed from there** in a **shocked** state**, with tears flowing from his eyes. Rabbi Ḥiyya was shaken and wept. He said: “Happy is the portion of the righteous in that world, and happy is** [Rabbi Shimon] **Bar Yoḥai that he merited this. With regard to him it is stated: “That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance and that I may fill their treasuries”** (Proverbs 8:21).

Explanation: The Messiah left Rabbi Shimon’s academy **“with tears flowing down his eyes,”** out of his great longing for the complete redemption. For this reason, **“Rabbi Ḥiyya was shaken”** as well.

**61. “In the beginning. Rabbi Shimon etc.” “In the beginning.” Rabbi Shimon began** his discourse with the following exposition**: “I placed My words in your mouth”** (Isaiah 51:16). **How much must a person toil in the Torah day and night, because the Holy One, blessed be He, listens to the voices of those who are engaged in the Torah. With each word that is renewed in the Torah, by means of that person who labors in the Torah, He fashions one firmament.**

Explanation: The Holy One, blessed be He, gave His power of speech into the mouths of the righteous, as He declares: **You are with Me, to partner with Me. Just I fashioned the heaven and earth with My speech, as it is stated: “By the word of the Lord were the heavens made”** (Psalms 33:6)**, the same applies to you.** So too, the righteous will create heaven by the power of their speech. With that, Rabbi Shimon began his discourse on the verse: **“In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth”** (Genesis 1:1). **“Created”** is a sealed word, a language of **closing rather than opening**, as stated above**.** It must be understood why He fashioned them in a sealed state. He says that He did so in order to place the completion of the rectification of heaven and earth in the speech of the righteous, thereby rendering them partners with Him in the creation of heaven and earth. This is why [Rabbi Shimon] cites the verse: **“I placed My words in your mouth.”**
It can be explained that here there are two aspects of the renewal of heaven and earth, which He placed in the mouths of the righteous:

1. To rectify the sin of Adam the first [man], for the Emanator fashioned the rectification of heaven and earth in a lofty form before the sin of Adam the first [man]. The verses of the act of creation explain that Ze’er Anpin and Nukba of Atzilut ascended to Arikh Anpin and Abba and Imma Ila'in , and Adam the first [man] ascended and enclothed [himself with] Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna and Ze’er Anpin and Nukba of Atzilut . Adam the first [man] had [the levels of] nefesh , ruaḥ and neshama of Atzilut , which is called **“supernal brightness,”** to the extent that Adam’s heel darkened the sphere of the sun (see Bava Batra 58a). After the sin of the Tree of Knowledge, he descended to this corporeal world (see Ḥagiga 12a) and now his nefesh , ruaḥ and neshama come to him from the three worlds of Beria , Yetzira , and Asiya of separation. The heaven and earth of Atzilut were reduced on [Adam's] account to [a level of] six extremities and a point, from the navel of Arikh Anpin and below. The [responsibility of this] rectification lies upon the righteous, to rectify all the impairments caused by the sin, and once again to renew the heaven and earth of Atzilut , which are Ze’er Anpin and Nukba , and to elevate them to Arikh Anpin and Abba and Imma Ila'in , as they were before the sin. The righteous themselves will be given back the supernal brightness of Adam the first [man], which is [the aspects of] nefesh , ruaḥ and neshama from the world of Atzilut .

2. Even Adam the first [man], before the sin, did not have all the perfection that the Emanator wished to grant him. Therefore, once the righteous rectify the sin of the Tree of Knowledge and attain the completion of nefesh , ruaḥ and neshama of Atzilut that Adam the first [man] had before the sin, a new task will be imposed upon them – to draw forth all the supernal minds that have never yet been in the world at all, which is the mystical meaning of: “No eye has seen it, God, aside from You” (Isaiah 64:3).

These worlds, which no eye has seen, and which the righteous will complete, are called **“new heavens and a new earth”** (Isaiah 65:17), for they are truly new, as they have never yet completely existed. This is not the case for the heavens and earth, which the righteous will renew and return to the state they were in at the act of creation, before the sin of Adam the first [man]. They are not considered a truly **new** heaven and earth, since they already existed once in the world, for the Emanator already rectified them Himself before the sin. Rather, they are **renewed**, as after they were impaired and nullified, they were renewed once again.

Consequently, these righteous are still not yet considered partners with the Holy One, blessed be He. Thus, the verse: **“I placed My words in your mouth,”** which Rabbi Shimon cites, refers to the supernal minds which Adam the first [man] also lacked, since they were truly innovated by the righteous and had not yet emerged from the Emanator. Accordingly, the righteous are considered actual partners [with the Emanator] with respect to [these worlds].

[The Zohar ] continues: **“The Holy One, blessed be He, listens to the voices of those who are engaged in the Torah. With each word that is renewed in the Torah etc.” ** Ze’er Anpin is called a “voice,” and its Nukba is called “speech.” When a righteous person engages in [the study of] the Torah, he raises feminine waters to Ze’er Anpin and Nukba through the voice and speech of his Torah [study], as the voice ascends to Ze’er Anpin and the speech ascends to the Nukba . This is the meaning of the statement: **“The Holy One, blessed be He, listens to the voice of those who are engaged in the Torah,”** that the voice of Torah ascends as feminine waters to Ze’er Anpin , which is called **“the Holy One, blessed be He.” “With each word that is renewed in the Torah etc. He fashions one firmament.” “Word”** means speech. Each and every word that is renewed **in the Torah** of the one engaged in Torah [study] ascends as feminine waters to the Nukba , which is called by the name “word” and “speech.” Through this, **one firmament** is fashioned. A firmament is the mystical meaning of the partition upon which is performed the pairing of the Holy One, blessed be He, with His Divine Presence. This is achieved by means of the feminine waters that the righteous raise through their engagement in the Torah.

As for the concept of innovation that is said [to be associated] with the “**word of the Torah**,” rather than saying an innovation in the **voice of the Torah**, this is because the Nukba requires a new construction of its Yesod for each pairing. This is because after each pairing, [the Nukba ] returns to a virgin state. By means of the feminine waters of the righteous, the aspect of Yesod in [the Nukba ] is continuously renewed, that is, the receptacle for the lights of Ze’er Anpin [are continuously renewed to receive those lights]. Therefore, [Rabbi Shimon specifically] says: **“With each word that is renewed in the Torah**, as the **word**, which is Malkhut , is actually renewed through the word of Torah of the righteous, for after every pairing its receptacle disappears once again, as explained.

**62. “We learned, at that time etc.” We learned: At that time, when a new word of Torah is innovated from a person’s mouth, that word ascends and meets the Holy One, blessed be He. The Holy One, blessed be He takes that word, kisses it, and crowns it with seventy carved and engraved crowns. The innovated word of wisdom ascends and sits on the head of the righteous one who is eternal life. From there, it flies and sails through seventy thousand worlds, ascending to the Atik Yomin** , which is the sefira of Keter **. All the words of the Atik Yomin are words of wisdom of the loftiest, concealed secrets.**

Explanation: **“That word ascends etc.”** This means to say, at the time when a person raises feminine waters through his word of Torah, that supernal **word**, which is the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin , **“ascends and meets the Holy One, blessed be He,”** to pair with Him.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“The Holy One, blessed be He takes that word, kisses it, and crowns it etc.”** Two aspects apply to each fusion of Ze’er Anpin and Nukba , and these are called “the fusion of kisses” and “the fusion of foundations.” As explained (above, in the section called “the mother lends,” 16), the name is not completed until He creates **“light for its light, and they were enclothed in one another”**; see there. The explanation of this is that apart from the height of Ḥokhma , a second [fusion through collision] is required [to generate a height of [the light of giving], so that the [column of the] height of Ḥokhma will be enclothed in the height of [the light of giving]. Accordingly, each incorporates two fusions: 1) For the [generation of the] height of Ḥokhma . This fusion is called “fusion of kisses,” as it [transpires] in the mouth of the head, that is, for the level of the head and the first three [ sefirot associated with the head]. 2) For the [generation of the] height of [the light of giving]. This fusion is called “fusion of foundations,” that is, for the height of [the light of giving]. This is the meaning of the statement that **“the Holy One, blessed be He takes that word,”** that is, the Nukba , **“kisses it,”** that is, a fusion of kisses for the [generation of] the height of the first three [ sefirot ], **“and crowns it,”** meaning a fusion of foundations, for the [generation of the] height of [the light of giving]. Then the [light of] Ḥokhma is enclothed in [the <<light of="" giving],="" and="" the="" <i="">Nukba is crowned with complete brains.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“With seventy carved and engraved crowns.”** The complete brains of the Nukba are called **“seventy crowns.”** The Nukba is the seventh day, and when [the Nukba ] receives from Ze’er Anpin , which is in the mystical meaning of tens, [the Nukba ] becomes **seventy**. The aspect of the brains is called **“crowns,”** and they are therefore called **“seventy crowns.”** [Rabbi Shimon] says that they are **“carved and engraved,”** that is, through the feminine waters of the righteous become a receptacle for these **seventy crowns**.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“The innovated word of wisdom ascends and sits on the head of the righteous one who lives for eternity.”** As explained above, there are two aspects to the renewal of heaven and earth which are Ze’er Anpin and Nukba : 1) To restore the crown to its former state before the sin of Adam the first [man]. You should know that concerning this renewal, the Nukba is called **“word of Torah,”** and this is what Rabbi Shimon has explained thus far. 2) The renewal of heaven and earth with respect to the supernal brains, which even Adam the first [man] did not attain. In this regard, the Nukba is called **“word of wisdom.”** He now proceeds to clarify [this second] innovation.

[Rabbi Shimon] says: **“The innovated word of wisdom ascends and sits on the head of the righteous one who lives for eternity.”** This is the mystical meaning of the Sages’ statement that “the righteous sit with their crowns upon their heads” ( Berakhot 17a). By means of the feminine waters of the righteous, who are already perfected with the supernal brightness of Adam the first [man], such as Rabbi Shimon and his colleagues, the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin ascends to become a crown for the head of the righteous, and that [righteous] is Ze’er Anpin with respect to its Yesod , which is the mystical meaning of the one who is eternal life. The meaning of this is as follows: The light of Ḥokhma is called “the light of ḥaya .” Since Ze’er Anpin can draw the light of ḥaya only by means of the Nukba (as stated in section 5 above, s. v. U-netziv ; see there), it is considered that [ Ze'er Anpin ] is alive only when it is in [its state of] pairing with the Nukba which is called **“world.”** In that state, [ Ze'er Anpin ] is therefore called **“the righteous one who is eternal life.”** It is also considered [in that state] that the Nukba is a crown over the head [of Ze'er Anpin ], that is, the brains which are called “crown” are from the Nukba , and [ Ze'er Anpin ] could not access [these brains] without [the Nukba ]. This is also the mystical meaning of: “He did not move from His fondness of her until calling her 'my mother'” (Midrash Song of Songs, end of chapter 3), since the consequence is considered the offspring of its cause. Since the Nukba was the cause of the [presence of the] light of ḥaya of Ze’er Anpin , in that respect the Nukba becomes his mother.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“From there, it flies and sails through seventy thousand worlds.”** After [the Nukba ] pairs with Ze’er Anpin in the mystical meaning of “a crown on the head of the righteous,” [the Nukba ] flies and ascends further up, that is, to Arikh Anpin . There, the seven sefirot of the Nukba are rectified in the mystical meaning of “seventy thousand worlds,” for the sefirot of Arikh Anpin are [counted] in the mystical meaning of ten thousand, as stated. From there [the Nukba ] ascends further, until the Atik Yomin , as [Rabbi Shimon] states: **“Ascending to the Atik Yomin ,”** for [the Nukba ] ascends from Arikh Anpin to the Atik Yomin . [Rabbi Shimon] calculates the ascents of Ze’er Anpin and Nukba one after the other, up to **Atik Yomin** , [all of] which is performed through the power of the feminine waters of the perfectly righteous. The fusion of the crown on the head of the righteous is achieved by [the Nukba ] ascending to Abba and Imma Ila'in , and from there [the Nukba ascends to Arikh Anpin in the mystical meaning of “seventy thousand worlds,” and from there to the Atik , which is the ultimate goal.

[Rabbi Shimon] continues: **“All the words of the Atik Yomin are words of wisdom of the loftiest, concealed secrets.”** Here [Rabbi Shimon] clarifies the quality of the brains that are bestowed upon the Nukba through its ascent to the Atik Yomin . He says that all the words of the Atik Yomin , that is, all the levels that are received from the Atik Yomin , are **“words of wisdom of the loftiest, concealed secrets,”** that is, they are the aspect of the first three [ sefirot ] of Ḥokhma . For **“words of wisdom [ Ḥokhma ]”** refers to the level of Ḥokhma , and **“the loftiest, concealed secrets”** are the first three [ sefirot ] of Ḥokhma . These are revealed only by ascending to the place of the **Atik Yomin** and not below it.

**63. “And that sealed word etc.” And that sealed word that was innovated here,** in this world, **when it ascends it connects to those words of the Atik Yomin , ascending and descending with them, and enters eighteen concealed worlds, which “no eye has seen it, God, aside from You.” They emerge from there and wander, and they come full and whole, and present themselves before the Atik Yomin . At that time, the Atik Yomin smells that word, and it is more pleasing to him than anything. He** then **takes that word and crowns it with 370, 000 crowns, and that word** of a new innovation in the Torah **wanders, ascending and descending, and one firmament is fashioned from it.**

Explanation: At the time of the ascent of the Nukba to the ** Atik Yomin **, [the Nukba ] is incorporated in the [fusion through collision] that is there. [The Nukba ] raises returning light and draws direct light from the Atik Yomin . **“Ascending”** means that [the Nukba ] raises returning light from below upwards. **“Descending”** means that [the Nukba ] draws the direct light from above to below, at which point [the Nukba ] receives the aforementioned wisdom of the loftiest, concealed secrets. When he says **“with them,”** this indicates that [the Nukba ] is incorporated with the returning light and the direct light that are in the Atik itself.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“And enters eighteen concealed worlds, which ‘no eye has seen it, God, aside from You. ’”** This [fusion through collision] that is performed in the Atik also takes place upon the Yesod of Atik that is there, and it is also **“the righteous one who lives for eternity,”** like Yesod of Ze’er Anpin at its ascent to Abba and Imma Ila'in , as stated above. The difference is that regarding Yesod of Atik , “no eye has seen it, God, aside from You.” The [fusion through collision] of Yesod is performed on the partition in the mystical meaning of collision. [This collision] raises the returning light in order to enclothe the direct light, as is known. Now below, in the Abba and Imma (father and mother), the partition is considered like wings that cover the supernal light when [the supernal light] is rebuffed backwards. This indicates that [the wings, an aspect of the partition, ] contain the force of judgment, as this is the mystical meaning of how every returning light is called “light of judgment.”

[However, ] this is not the case for the Yesod of Atik , regarding which it is stated: “Your Teacher shall not hide Himself any more etc.” (Isaiah 30:10). Although the partition raises returning light from below upwards, the aspect of wings is not present. [This Yesod of Atik Yomin ] is therefore called **“eighteen concealed worlds, which ‘no eye has seen it, God, aside from You. ’”** In other words, [at that level, there are no longer wings there that cover [it] from a foreign eye, since there are no judgments there, but **“no eye has seen it, God, aside from You.”** Understand this well. For the level that is from below upwards is called “concealed,” yet it is in the form of **“no eye has seen it etc.”**

[The Zohar ] continues: **“They emerge from there and wander, and they come full and whole.”** [The phrase] **“they emerge from there”** means [they emerge] from the mystical meaning of the [fusion through collision] upon the partition, which is called **“eighteen concealed worlds, which ‘no eye has etc. ’”** The term **“wander”** means that [the partition] raises the returning light from below upwards. **“They come”** means that the direct light is drawn down from above to below, and then they are **“full and whole,”** filled with direct light, **from the wisdom of the loftiest, concealed secrets**. They are “whole” with respect to the returning light, as it contains no judgments but is entirely complete mercy, equal to the direct light. They then **“present themselves before the Atik Yomin ,”** as they are ready to enclothe the Atik Yomin .

[The Zohar ] continues: **“At that time, the Atik Yomin smells that word, and it is more pleasing to him than anything.” “Smells”** is the mystical meaning of contentment of the spirit, since this great and lofty [fusion through collision] brings exceedingly sublime contentment of the spirit to the Atik Yomin . This is because every single one of the worlds and all of their merit are then incorporated in the Nukba . This is the meaning of the statement: **“And it is more pleasing to him than anything [ mi-kula ],”** because that contentment comes to [ Atik Yomin ] “from all [ mi-kula ],” from all of the worlds at once, since this is the utter perfection, and the height upon which the worlds were created.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“He takes that word and crowns it with 370, 000 crowns.”** That is, [ Atik Yomin ] then bestows upon [the Nukba ] the sublime brains of Atik himself, which are Ḥokhma , Bina , Tiferet , and Malkhut , each of which amounts to one hundred thousand, since the sefirot of Atik are one hundred thousand each, as stated. However, the difference is because of the upper thirty of Ḥokhma , as there it is the mystical meaning of: “He was the most honorable of the thirty, but did not attain to the first three” (see II Samuel 2:23). In other words, even though [the Nukba ] also receives and is honored by the first three [ sefirot ] of Ḥokhma of Atik , which are the upper thirty thousand [of Atik Yomin ], as stated earlier, nevertheless, the Nukba cannot actually ascend and enclothe these thirty thousand themselves. The reason is that if [the Nukba ] were to enclothe those thirty thousand as well, the Nukba would be nullified within him, like a candle before a torch. Therefore, [the Nukba ] receives from the Atik only 370, 000 crowns, that is, four hundred thousand minus thirty thousand, for that stated reason.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“that word wanders, ascending and descending, and one firmament is fashioned from it.” “Wanders”** means that it flies upwards; **“wanders, ascending”** means that it raises returning light from below upwards. **“And descending” –** with the returning light that it raises, it descends with direct light from above to below. **“And one firmament is fashioned from it”** – by means of the enclothing of the direct light by the returning light, one firmament is fashioned there. For after the [fusion through collision] is performed upon that partition, which was established in Malkhut in order to raise the returning light that reached the Nukba through good deeds [of the created beings] and feminine waters (which the [created beings] raised in order to bestow contentment upon their Maker, as stated) – [the partition] becomes a firmament through which the righteous attain that height of fusion that was performed upon [that partition]. The idea is that when the level descends to the righteous through the firmament, [the level] is enclothed in a garment that is drawn from that **firmament**, which is an aspect of the returning light that inverts from the firmament to below, together with the direct light from the firmament and above. Thus, [this height] is available for the attainment of the righteous who are enclothed in one another.

The meaning of this is as follows: Those righteous who have merited that wholeness, to raise feminine waters for that lofty fusion, no longer have any aspect of receiving for their own needs. The feminine waters that they raised was [purely] in order to bestow, not to receive. Consequently, with their good deeds and the [resulting] feminine waters, the [righteous] rectify the partition of the Nukba , rendering her fit for this great fusion. The fitness [for the fusion] itself is the mystical meaning of the returning light that ascends from the partition of the Nukba upward, since anything that ascends from below upwards is the mystical meaning of bestowing, and the rebuffing of receiving for oneself. Then the fusion through collision with the supernal light is performed, and the supernal light is enclothed in a garment of ascending returning light.

Now, the light that descends from above to below, and which is enclothed in returning light, comes to be received by the lower one, that is, for that righteous person who raised the feminine waters, because when anything comes from above to below, this means that it comes to be received. Since the supernal light passes to the lower [level] through the firmament, [the supernal light] takes with it the aspect of the clothing of the returning light from the firmament, and the lower [righteous person] receives the supernal light within this garment. This means that even after the height comes to be received by the lower one, [that person] only benefits from the supernal light that descends to him according to the measure of bestowal of contentment upon his Maker, that is, according to the measure of the clothing of the returning light, which enclothes the supernal light. This is considered “receiving in order to bestow.” [The righteous person] does not receive anything if it does not include a bestowal upon his Maker. Therefore, the receiving [of the supernal light] is enclothed within the bestowal [upon his Maker], direct light in returning light. This is why [the Zohar ] emphasizes that **“that word wanders, ascending and descending, and one firmament is fashioned from it.”** In other words, [the word] is received by the lower [beings] only through the firmament, that is, [the supernal light] with its enclothing garment, as stated.

**64. “And likewise, each and every word etc.” And likewise, each and every word of wisdom are fashioned into firmaments, established in full existence before the Atik Yomin , who calls them “new heavens,”** that is, **renewed heavens,** which are **sealed secrets of the supernal wisdom. And all the rest of the innovated words of Torah,** which are not from the supernal Ḥokhma , **stand before the Holy One, blessed be He, and ascend and become the lands of the living, and descend and are crowned into one land. Everything is renewed and becomes a new land by** the strength of **that word which was innovated in the Torah.**

Explanation: The righteous proceed in this manner, continuously raising feminine waters and drawing those sublime levels from the Atik Yomin by means of these firmaments that were fashioned through the supernal [fusion through collision]. The mystical meaning of the **“new heavens”** is made from those firmaments, which are renewed at the level of the Atik Yomin , as stated. Therefore, those high attainments are called **“sealed secrets of the supernal wisdom,”** because they come enclothed in the garment that is drawn from the firmaments.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“All the rest of the** [innovated] **words of Torah etc. into one land. Everything is renewed and becomes a new land.”** In each level, there are [the aspects of] Ḥokhma , Bina , Tiferet , and Malkhut . Thus far, the discussion was only in reference to **“the secrets of wisdom [ Ḥokhma ],”** not of Bina , Ze’er Anpin [which is Tiferet ], or Malkhut in each level. [Rabbi Shimon] thus says: **“And become the lands of the living,”** meaning that [these words] all become Bina , which is called “the land of the living.” They descend **“and are crowned into one land,”** that is, to Malkhut , which is called simply “land.” **“Everything is renewed and becomes a new land,”** because the Malkhut was crowned and received all the levels of the lands of the living, which are Bina , and by means of this [receiving], the Malkhut ascended to become Bina .

[ Malkhut ] is now called **“a new land,”** since what was previously Malkhut is now Bina . This is the mystical meaning of: “The Ban (or bet-nun ) will in the future be Sag (or samekh-gimmel ), and the Mah (or mem-heh ) will be Ab (or ayin-bet ).” The heavens are Ze’er Anpin , and now at the level of the Atik Yomin , they are in [the state of] **“the secrets of the supernal wisdom [ Ḥokhma ].”** Thus, the Mah , which is Ze’er Anpin , becomes Ab , that is, Ḥokhma ; and “land,” which is Nukba of Ze’er Anpin , becomes Sag , that is, Bina . It follows that the mystical meaning of **“new heavens and a new earth”** is Mah and Ban that were nullified and have become Ab Sag .

**65. “And with regard to this, it is written etc.” And with regard to this, it is stated: “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I make, shall remain before Me etc.”** (Isaiah 66:22)**. It is not written “I made,” but “make,”** in the present tense, because **He is always making** new heavens and earth **from those innovations and secrets of the Torah. With regard to this it is stated: “I placed My words in your mouth and have covered you in the shadow of My hand, that I may plant heavens and lay the foundations of earth”** (Isaiah 51:16). **It does not say “the heavens,” but “heavens**,” without the definitive article, since it is not referring to the actual heavens, but to renewed heavens, fashioned out of words of Torah**.**

Explanation: **“It is not written ‘I made, ’ but ‘make’ etc.”** This teaches that one should not err in interpreting the phrase **“new heavens and new earth”** as referring to an establishment that is performed and innovated once only, as that is not the case. Rather, they involve a continuous process. The righteous, who have already been perfected in the supernal brightness, are constantly fashioning new heavens and earth. This is the mystical meaning of: **“They go from strength to strength”** (Psalms 84:8; end of Berakhot , 64a). [Rabbi Shimon] cites a proof for this, that it is stated: **“For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I make,”** and **it is not written “I made,” but “make.”** This illustrates that these heavens and earth are perpetually renewed through the Torah innovations of the completely righteous. [Rabbi Shimon] likewise brings a proof from the phrase **“that I may plant heavens,”** since if this was referring to a one-time act, it should have stated “that I may plant the heavens,” with the definitive article. The fact that it states “heavens” implies that it is an ongoing activity.

**66. “Rabbi Elazar said, what is etc.” Rabbi Elazar said: What is** [the meaning of] **“and have covered you in the shadow of My hand”** (Isaiah 51:16)**? He replied: When the Torah was given to Moses, many multitudes of supernal angels came to burn him with the flames of their mouths, but the Holy One, blessed be He, covered him. Now, when the Torah innovation ascends, is crowned, and stands before the Holy One, blessed be He, He covers that word and covers that person, so that he will not be known to them, but to the Holy One, blessed be He, and they will not envy him, until that that word is fashioned into new heavens and new earth. This is the meaning of the verse: “And have covered you in the shadow of My hand, that I may plant heavens and lay the foundations of earth.” From here** [we learn] **that everything which is covered from the eye counts toward the supernal purpose. This is the meaning of the verse: “And have covered you in the shadow of My hand.” Why was he covered and hidden from the eye? For the supernal purpose. This is the meaning of the verse: “That I may plant heavens and lay the foundations of earth,” as we learned**, that is, so that new heavens and earth would sprout from it**.**

Explanation: **“And have covered you in the shadow of My hand etc.”** This is referring to the aforementioned garment, which is drawn from the firmament and which enclothes and covers the height of the brains (as stated above, s. v. Hahi mila ; see there). This clothing is the aspect of **“shadow”** that covers the brains and hides them from foreign eyes, and they are known solely to the Holy One, blessed be He. [Rabbi Shimon] proceeds to explain the reason for this [covering], that it is in order to conceal those great levels from the ministering angels, so that they will not envy [the righteous person]. This envy of the angels is because they are pure of substance, and thus when they look at a righteous person, they find a kind of inferiority in him, and envy him for the high level he has attained. Subsequently, the prosecuting forces grasp hold of that inferiority that the angels discovered in him.

Consequently, when the level is enclothed in that garment of the firmament, this garment measures the level [to be received by the righteous person], so that [the righteous person] will not receive too much of [of the brains of the level], only that which is for the benefit of the Supernal One, may He be blessed. [The righteous person] is thereby protected from the envy of the angels, for then the righteous can be guarded from impairing the level, exactly like the angels.

[Rabbi Shimon] thus states: **“Every word that is covered from the eye ascends for the supernal benefit.”** [Rabbi Shimon] is alluding to the way that the eye sees and the heart lusts, and thus [a person] cannot guard his thoughts so that they will remain clean and provide only contentment to his Creator, but rather [a person] also receives benefit for himself. However, that which is **“covered from the eye,”** that is, which is enclothed in the garment of the firmament, will assuredly not receive more than that which ascends for the benefit of the Supernal One, may He be blessed. This is the meaning of his statement: **“Why was it covered and hidden from the eye? For the supernal benefit,”** as explained.

**67. “And to say to Zion, you are My people” “And to say to Zion: You are My people”** (Isaiah 51:16)**. “And to say,”** that is, **to those gates and words that are marked one above the other**, that is, to the Torah innovations**: “You are My people.” Do not read: “You are My people [ ami ],”** with a pataḥ vowel under the letter ayin , **but rather: “You are with Me [ imi ],”** with a ḥirik under the ayin , meaning **“to be a partner with Me.” Just as I made heaven and earth with My speech, as it is stated: “By the word of the Lord were the heavens made”** (Psalms 33:6)**, so too you**, with your words of wisdom, have made new heavens and earth**. Happy are those who toil in the Torah.**

Explanation: The aspect of receiving is called **“gates,”** as gates are open to receive, while the aspect of giving through the feminine waters is called **“words,”** as stated above. [Rabbi Shimon] adds that they **“are marked one above the other,”** meaning that they are enclothed in one another, which thereby marks them.

**68. “And if you say that a word etc.” “And if you say that a word of innovation from any person,** even **if he does not know** what he is saying, **has this effect,** [then] **come and see: One who is not proficient in the secrets of Torah, and innovated words whose truth he does not properly know, that innovation ascends and there emerges to that word a duplicitous man who speaks lies, from the female of the great deep. He leaps five hundred parasangs to receive that word, and he takes it and walks with the word to his female, and fashions a false firmament within her, which is called “emptiness”** [ tohu ]**.**

Explanation: As you are already aware, the mystical meaning of the feminine waters that the righteous raise in order to bring contentment to their Maker, that is, **“for the supernal benefit”** (section 66, above), is called **words of Torah** that were innovated. They are innovated by the supernal [fusion through collision], and the [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba receive new brains through them, until they thereby merit the mystical meaning of **“plant heavens and lay the foundations of earth** etc.” They thus become partners with the Holy One, blessed be He, since heaven and earth are renewed through their words, as stated.

[The Zohar ] continues: However, **“one who is not proficient in the secrets of Torah,”** that is, he is not versed in the ways of God, to know how to guard himself from impairing the higher levels. Now, he says to himself that his aim is **for the supernal purpose**, but he is fooling himself, for he does not realize that it is his responsibility to know for certain that his intention is not, God forbid, for his own needs. His punishment is grave indeed, for he gives power to the kelippot **to kill people**, as the author proceeds to explain. This is the meaning of: **“And innovated words whose truth he does not properly know.”** That is, he raises feminine waters for the supernal fusion, and yet he does not fully understand that this is indeed the case. It thus turns out that this **“duplicitous man who speaks lies”** minimizes and abuses **that word**, as [Rabbi Shimon] further elaborates.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“A duplicitous man who speaks lies, from the female of the great deep.”** There are male and female in the kelippot as well. The male is called **“false,”** and the female is called **“lies.”** The explanation of this is that the male kelippa is not as evil as the female. Left to himself, [the male kelippa ] would not trick people into lying in the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. On the contrary, it would appear that he speaks well, or so it seems. However, he has an evil eye, in the mystical meaning of the verse: “Do not eat bread of he who has an evil eye…eat and drink, he says to you; but his heart is not with you” (Proverbs 23:6-7). Whoever is ensnared by him will bear the name of God in vain, for he is separated from the Lord and cannot receive any shefa . This is the mystical meaning of the Sages’ statement: “Whoever is arrogant, the Holy One, Blessed be He, says: He and I cannot reside in a single abode” (see Sota 5a). Since his intention is towards his own needs, to brag and boast and the like, he is ensnared in the domain of that evil-eyed one. The result is that the feminine waters which [such a person] raises do not draw forth any shefa from above, and he employs the name of God in vain. For this reason, the male kelippa is called **false**, since the Holy One, blessed be He, cannot become attached to that man, to reside together with him in one abode.

The female of the kelippa is called **lies**, for after that man has become ensnared in the net of the male, who is called **false**, that male [ kelippa ] has the power to mate with his female. She is an evil and bitter kelippa , which forges the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, and utters lies with it. She subsequently descends and incites, and then ascends and accuses, and takes [the person's] soul from him.

[The male kelippa ] is therefore called **“a duplicitous man,”** since at first “eat and drink, he says to you,” that is, so that [the person] will raise the feminine waters to the Holy One, blessed be He, and draw forth shefa for the needs of the Most High, and [the male kelippa ] seems to [the person] as though he is from the side of holiness. Subsequently, through the power of his **falsehood**, [the male kelippa ] mates with the **“female of the great deep,”** and with her **lies** he takes [the person's] soul and kills him. This is the meaning of: **“A duplicitous man who speaks lies, from the female of the great deep,”** since he duplicitously transforms into **speaking lies** only through the strength of the **female of the great deep** with whom he associates, not from himself.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“He leaps five hundred parasangs to receive that word.”** Explanation: The [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba of impurity only have six extremities and a point at their root, that is, they are only an opposite [set of the aspects of] six extremities and a point of the [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba of holiness, and they have no place or strength to attach to Bina . However, by means of **“that word,”** that is, the feminine waters that the [being from] below raises, he gives the male of impurity the strength to leap over the seven lower [ sefirot ] of Bina that are [normally] drawn into [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba of holiness. [These lower seven] are essentially only five sefirot : Ḥesed , Gevura , Tiferet , Netzaḥ , and Hod . They are called “five hundred parasangs” because the sefirot of Bina are counted in the unit of hundreds, as is known. He thus says: **“He leaps five hundred parasangs to receive that word,”** because immediately upon the ascent of the feminine waters, [the male kelippa ] attained the power to leap into a place that is not his, that is, the five lower sefirot : Ḥesed , Gevura , Tiferet , Netzaḥ , and Hod , which are called five hundred parasangs. “To receive that word” is referring to the feminine waters that are raised by the man who did not properly know if his intention was to provide contentment to his Maker.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“And walks with the word to his female, and fashions a false firmament within her, which is called ‘emptiness’** [ tohu ]**.”** In other words, he mates with his female **“of the great deep,”** over these feminine waters, and draws lights of holiness to him, to his portion and to his construction, similar to the new heavens of holiness that are fashioned by the feminine waters of holiness, as stated. These heavens that he drew forth through his mating are called **“a false firmament,”** with regard to the male, while with respect to the association with the female of the great deep it is called a firmament **of emptiness**. **“Emptiness”** is the name of the male, and the name of the female is “deep.” This is the meaning of the statement: **“And fashions a false firmament,”** with the strength of his own self, **“which is called emptiness,”** by the strength of his association with the **deep**, the female.

**69. “And he flies in that firmament etc.” “And he flies in that** false **firmament, that duplicitous man, six thousand parasangs in one go. Once this false firmament stands still, a woman of harlotry immediately emerges and holds that false firmament and participates in it. From there she goes forth and kills several thousands and myriads, since while she is in that firmament she has the permission and ability to fly and to traverse the entire world in an instant.**

Explanation: These brains that were drawn out to [the person] in that **false firmament** are from the Sitra Aḥara that corresponds to the Ḥokhma of holiness, whose units are the thousands. This is the meaning of **“he flies in that firmament,”** that he soars and is gripped by it, for **“six thousand parasangs in one go”** – in the six sefirot : Ḥesed , Gevura , Tiferet , Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod , of Ḥokhma . These are called **six thousand parasangs,** as they are from Ḥokhma .

[The Zohar ] continues: **“Once this false firmament stands still, a woman of harlotry immediately emerges and holds that false firmament and participates in it.”** In other words, after the completion of the new heavens of the male kelippa , which are called only by the name **“false,”** the **“female of the great deep”** then reveals her power. Her power attacks the firmament, in order to lie in the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, and she proceeds to fly in the firmament, which is then called **“the firmament of emptiness,”** as stated above (in the previous section).

[The Zohar ] continues: **“From there she goes forth and kills... since while she is in that firmament, she has the permission and ability to fly and to traverse the entire world in an instant.”** While she participates in that firmament, she grows stronger and larger than the level of the male. The male grows only to the six extremities of Ḥokhma , which are six thousand parasangs, as stated above, while the female grows by means of [the male] through ten complete sefirot , which is a whole world. This is the meaning of **“she has the permission and ability to fly and to traverse the entire world,** that is, a whole world in ten sefirot . **“In an instant”** is the mystical meaning of the teaching: “How long is His anger? A moment” ( Berakhot 7a). She therefore has the power to kill thousands and myriads, in the mystical meaning of the verse: “For she has cast down many slain” (Proverbs 7:26). Rabbi Shimon has thus explained to us that “God made one thing corresponding to the other” (Ecclesiastes 7:14) – just as the new heavens and earth for holiness are constantly being built by the feminine waters of the righteous, so too the heavens and earth for the kelippot are continuously being constructed through the feminine waters of those who do not know how to serve properly the Holy One, blessed be He.

**70. “And with regard to this, it is written etc.” “And with regard to this, it is stated: “Woe to them who draw iniquity with false cords”** (Isaiah 5:18)**. “Iniquity” is the male. “And sin as it were with a cart rope”** (Isaiah 5:18)**. What is “sin”? This is the female,** that is, the aforementioned woman of harlotry, **who is called “sin.” It**, the sinner, **drags that which is called “iniquity**,” that is, the male, **with these false cords, and subsequently, “sin as it were with a cart rope.”** He pulls **on that female who is called “sin,” as she grows stronger there, to fly and kill people. Therefore, “for she has cast down many slain”** (Proverbs 7:26)**. Who has cast down? She, that “sin,” who kills people. Who caused this? A student who has not attained the ability to issue rulings, and** [yet] **he issues** [them]**. May the Merciful One save us!**

Explanation: As we wrote above, the male is not as evil as the female, because he imagines himself to be holy, in the mystical meaning of the verse: “Eat and drink, he says to you; but his heart is not with you” (Proverbs 23:7). He is therefore called **“false.”** However, for this very reason he is highly capable of catching people in his net. Once they have fallen into his net, he comes and mates with the female, at which point there is **“sin as it were with a cart rope,”** for she drags him into the great deep. This is how the verse **“woe to them who draw iniquity with false cords”** should be interpreted. The **“false”** one only ties a person with cords and traps him, and then casts him down before his female. At this stage, **“sin as it were with a cart rope”** – the **“sin”** casts him into the great deep and kills him. This is the meaning of: **“that ‘sin, ’ who kills people.”**

**71. “Rabbi Shimon said etc.” Rabbi Shimon said to the colleagues: “Please, do not let a word of Torah emerge from your mouths that you do not know or have not heard from a tree that is suitably large, so that you will not cause that sin of needlessly killing masses of people.” They all declared: “May the Merciful One save us; may the Merciful One save us!”**

Explanation: **“A word of Torah etc.”** In other words, if you know it of your own accord, that is all well and good, but if not, you must listen how to serve God **“from a tree that is suitably large,”** that is, from a great person who can be relied upon, **“so that you will not cause”** etc.

**72. “Come and see, with the Torah etc.” Come and see: The Holy One, blessed be He, created the world with the Torah. [The Sages] established this, as it is stated: “Then I was by Him as a nursling; and I was daily all delight”** (Proverbs 8:30)**.** This is referring to the Torah, which the Holy One, blessed be He, played with for two thousand years before the world was created (as stated in section 22, above). **He looked at her once, twice, three, and four times, and then He spoke to them. Ultimately, he performed a deed upon her, in order to teach people not to come to err through her, as it says: “Then He saw it, and declared it; He established it, and also searched it out. And to man He said”** (Job 28:27-28)**.** “He saw it” is the first time; “declared it” is the second; “He established it” is the third; “and also searched it out” is the fourth time. Then He spoke to them, as it is stated: “And to man He said.”

**73. “And corresponding to these four times etc.” And corresponding to these four times, as it is stated: “Then He saw it”; “and told it”; He established it”; “and also inquired after it,” the Holy One, blessed be He, created what He created. Before He performed His action, He first brought forth four words, as it is stated: Bereshit bara Elohim et ** [“In the beginning God created”]**, which are four, and** it is **subsequently** written**: HaShamayim [“the heavens”]. These correspond to the four times that the Holy One, blessed be He, looked in the Torah before He brought out His action for His labor.**

Explanation: **“And corresponding to these four times etc.”** Those four times are the mystical meaning of Ḥokhma , Bina , Tiferet , and Malkhut : **“Then He saw it”** is Ḥokhma ; **“and declared it”** is Bina ; **“He established it”** is Ze’er Anpin ; “and also inquired after it” is Malkhut . After those four enclothings, **“the Holy One, blessed be He, created what He created.”** This is also alluded to by the first four words of the Torah: ** Bereshit ** is Ḥokhma ; ** bara ** is Bina ; ** Elohim ** is Ze’er Anpin ; ** et ** is Malkhut . After those four enclothings, the heavens were created.

**74. “Rabbi Elazar was etc.” Rabbi Elazar was going to see Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Shimon, son of Lakunya, his father-in-law, and Rabbi Abba was accompanying him. A certain man was driving their donkeys behind them**, that is, he was leading their donkeys**. Rabbi Abba said: “Let us open the doors of Torah, as now is the time and the hour to rectify ourselves in our ways.”** “Driving” [ ta’in ] means “poking,” just as medukarim (“wounded, Jeremiah 37:10) is translated into Aramaic as meta’anin . By extension, the term refers to donkey drivers, as they would poke the donkeys with a needle to speed them up.

**75. “Rabbi Elazar began etc.” Rabbi Elazar began** his discourse **and said** the following exposition**: “You shall keep My Sabbaths”** (Leviticus 19:30)**. Come and see: The Holy One, blessed be He, created the world in six days. On each and every day, He revealed His action and inserted His power on that day. When did He reveal His action and insert His power? On the fourth day, since those first three days were all hidden and not revealed. Once the fourth day arrived, He brought out the action and strength of all of them.**

Explanation: **“On that day”** – that is, the day of **Shabbat.** The six weekdays, which are Ḥesed , Gevura , Tiferet , Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod , reveal the completion of their works and their power on the day of Shabbat, which is Malkhut .

**“When did He reveal His action and insert His power? On the fourth day etc.”** [Rabbi Elazar] previously stated that “on each and every day, He revealed His action and inserted His power on **the day of Shabbat”,** yet here he says that this occurred only **“on the fourth day.”** This requires explanation. The idea is that Malkhut is called “fourth” and “seventh” – **fourth to the patriarchs**, which are Ḥesed , Gevura , and Tiferet , and **seventh to the children**, Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod . Rabbi Shimon accordingly said (section 4, above) that **“the flowers,”** which are Ḥesed , Gevura , and Tiferet , **“appeared on the earth” on the third day; “the time of singing has come,” this is the fourth day,** when the Malkhut was diminished and ascended for a second gestation; see there. Thus, the Malkhut was emanated from Ḥesed , Gevura , and Tiferet on the third day and was established on the fourth day by means of Netzaḥ of Ze’er Anpin , which is the fourth day. Consequently, in this respect she is called **“fourth to the patriarchs.”** [Rabbi Shimon] subsequently states there: **“In our land – this is the day of Shabbat, which is like the land of the living.”** Thus, the Malkhut , which is called **“land,”** is an expression of the **day of Shabbat**, which is **“seventh to the children.”** It is this matter, of the fourth and seventh, which is clarified here.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“Since those first three days were all hidden and not revealed etc.”** As long as a level lacks Malkhut , [the level] is considered hidden and unknown. When [the level] attains Malkhut , [the level] attains its wholeness. This is the mystical meaning of the six days of work and Shabbat. [One could think] that the six days of work should be considered more important than the day of Shabbat, since Ḥesed , Gevura , Tiferet , Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod , which are the six days of work, are more important than the Malkhut , which is the day of Shabbat. However, the [correct] explanation is that each week is a separate level, which lacks Malkhut during the days of work. Therefore, the level is hidden and contains no holiness, since with the absence of Malkhut the first three lights are absent, as stated earlier. It is only upon the revelation of Malkhut in that level, that is, upon the arrival of the day of Shabbat, that the holiness is revealed in the entire level, that is, in the six days of work as well, and the holiness permeates the whole of that week. The same applies to the six days of creation: When **the first three days,** which are Ḥesed , Gevura , and Tiferet , were emanated before the revelation of Malkhut , they were **hidden,** without the revelation of the holiness within them. When the Malkhut was emanated, which occurred on the fourth day, the holiness of all four days was then revealed. This is the meaning of the statement: **“Once the fourth day arrived, He brought out the action and strength of all of them,”** that is, the holiness was revealed through the work and power of all four days, since Malkhut completes the level.

**76. “For fire, and water etc.” For fire, and water, and wind,** which are Ḥesed , Gevura , and Tiferet , and the mystical meaning of the first three days**, even though they are three supernal foundations,** that is, the three sefirot Ḥesed , Gevura , and Tiferet , **they were all suspended, and the complete work was not revealed until the earth**, which is the mystical meaning of Malkhut , **revealed them. Then the work of each and every one of them became known.**

**77. “And if you say, etc.” And if you say: But it is the third day, as it is stated: “Let the earth put forth grass”** (Genesis 1:11) **and it is stated: “And the earth brought forth** (grass**,”** Genesis 1:12)**.** This shows that the revelation of the work of the earth, which is Malkhut , was on the third day. He answers: **Rather, even though this is written on the third day,** which is the mystical meaning of Tiferet , **it was** [actually] **the fourth day**, which is the mystical meaning of Malkhut **. It was included in the third day so that they**, Tiferet and Malkhut , **are one, without separation. Subsequently, the fourth day revealed its work, of bringing out the craftsman for the labor of each and every one of them,** of Ḥesed , Gevura , and Tiferet , **because the fourth day is the fourth leg of the supernal throne,** which is Bina , whose four legs are Ḥesed , Gevura , Tiferet , and Malkhut **.**

Explanation: Since Malkhut reveals the holiness of the three days, [ Malkhut ] ascended and was incorporated in the third day, in order to reveal the unification upon them, that is, as **“they are one, without separation.”**

[The Zohar ] continues: **“Subsequently, the fourth day etc.”** On the fourth day, the Malkhut served as the completion of only the first three days, and afterwards three more days emerged, which are Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod . This is the meaning of the statement: **“Subsequently, the fourth day revealed its work, of bringing out the craftsman for the labor of each and every one of them.”** Once the holiness had been revealed over the first three days, which are Ḥesed , Gevura , and Tiferet , called the patriarchs, who are the main aspect of Ze’er Anpin , then Ze’er Anpin , who is the craftsman, went out for his **“labor,”** and the children – who are called Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod , the last three of the six days of creation – were emanated. This is **“because the fourth day is the fourth leg of the supernal throne,”** as Ze’er Anpin is considered a throne for Bina . Just as a throne is not ready until its fourth leg is finished, so too the Ze’er Anpin is not completed until the Malkhut is revealed in it on the fourth day. He thus could not emanate the three days, Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod , until after [ Malkhut ’s] completion [of the first three days].

**78. “And all the actions of all of them, etc.” And all the actions of all of them, whether the first three days,** which are Ḥesed , Gevura , and Tiferet , **or the last three days, ** Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod , **were dependent on the day of Shabbat**, which is Malkhut of the level of the first three [ sefirot ] and the whole completion [of that level]**. This is** the meaning of **that which is stated: “And on the seventh day God finished His work”** (Genesis 2:2)**. This is Shabbat, and this is the fourth leg of the throne.** This means to say that Shabbat and the fourth day are both the aspect of Malkhut . [The difference is that] the fourth day is the Malkhut that is incorporated in Ze’er Anpin , in the Tiferet [of Ze’er Anpin ] from the chest and above, whereas the day of Shabbat is the mystical meaning of Malkhut in a [state of] fusion with Ze’er Anpin , face-to-face.

Explanation: **“And all the actions of all of them etc.”** That is, even though the first three days were completed through the fourth day, they were still not entirely completed through [the fourth day], as they **“were dependent on the day of Shabbat.”** Thus, on the day of Shabbat they were completed, **“whether the first three days,”** Ḥesed , Gevura , and Tiferet , **“or the last three days,”** Netzaḥ , Hod , and Yesod . This is the meaning of the verse: **“And on the seventh day God finished His work which He had made,”** that is, all six days, including the first three days.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“This is Shabbat, and this is the fourth leg of the throne.”** In other words, the seventh day is **Shabbat,** that is, seventh of the children. It is also **“the fourth leg of the throne,”** meaning that it also completes the patriarchs, and Shabbat is their fourth. The reason why the three days Ḥesed , Gevura , and Tiferet were not fully completed on the fourth day, but require the day of Shabbat to complete them, is that there was a diminution in Malkhut on the fourth day, which is called “the diminution of the moon.” As a result, [the Malkhut ] returned for a second gestation and its completeness was revealed on the day of Shabbat. Consequently, the day of Shabbat completed the first three days as well.

**79. “And if you say, if, etc.” And if you say: If so,** that Shabbat is Malkhut , **what is** the meaning of the verse**: “You shall keep My Sabbaths”** (Leviticus 19:30)**,** which are **two?** He answers: **the Shabbat of Shabbat eve,** which is Malkhut , **and the Shabbat of the actual Shabbat day**, which is Ze’er Anpin , which illuminates the Shabbat that is Malkhut . **They cannot be separated**, as they are united face-to-face and are called “two Sabbaths**.”**

Explanation: His question is as follows: According to the initial explanation, that the two Malkhut s, the fourth [day] and seventh [day], are each whole in themselves, the verse **“My Sabbaths”** is properly understood, as there are **two** [ Malkhut s]**,** the fourth and seventh. However, once you have said that [the first three days] are not [fully] completed through the fourth [day], but only after [the fourth] is incorporated in the seventh, then [that implies] they are [really] only one Shabbat. Why, then, does the verse state **“My Sabbaths,” two**, [which implies two separate Sabbaths]**?** He answers that it is referring to the aspects of Ze’er Anpin and Nukba that illuminate the holiness of the Shabbat. The day of Shabbat is the male, while the eve of Shabbat is the female. These are the two Sabbaths included in “My Sabbaths,” as they are actually **one, without separation.** Accordingly, the Ze’er Anpin is also called “Shabbat.” Understand this.

**80. “That donkey driver, etc.” That donkey driver who was driving** the donkeys **behind them said: “But what is** the meaning of: **‘And fear My sanctuary?’”** (Leviticus 19:30)**? [Rabbi Elazar] replied: “This is the sanctity of the Shabbat.” [The driver] responded: “And what is the sanctity of the Shabbat?” He said to [the driver]: “This is holiness that extends from above**, from the father and mother**.” [The driver] retorted: “If so, you have rendered the Shabbat as not holy in itself; rather, the holiness rests upon it from above**, from the father and mother**.” Rabbi Abba said: “That is indeed the case**, as it is stated: **‘And call the Sabbath a delight, and the holy of the Lord honorable’** (Isaiah 58:13)**. The Shabbat is mentioned separately, and ‘the holy of the Lord’ separately.” [The driver] said to [Rabbi Abba]: “If so, who is ‘the holy of the Lord’?” He replied: “It is the holiness that descends from above,** from the father and mother, **and resides over it**, the Shabbat**.” [The driver] retorted: “If the holiness that descends from above is called ‘honorable, ’ it appears that the Shabbat itself is not honorable, and** [yet] **it is stated: “And you shall honor it”** (Isaiah 58:13), which indicates that the Shabbat itself is honorable**. Rabbi Elazar said to Rabbi Abba: “Leave that man, as there is a word of wisdom in him, which we do not know.” They said to him: “You say.”**

Explanation: [The driver] asked [Rabbi Elazar]: **What is** the meaning of **“and fear My sanctuary?”** Since you maintain that the mystical meaning of Shabbat is the aspect of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , why does the verse call them **“My sanctuary,”** when only the father and mother are called holy?

He replied: **“The Shabbat is mentioned separately, and ‘the holy of the Lord’ separately.”** [Rabbi Elazar] proved to [the driver] from here that Shabbat itself is the aspect of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , **“as it is not holy”** in its own right, but because **“holiness from above”** is extended to it, that is, from Abba and Imma Ila’in , which are called **“holy.”** The aspect of extension from [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ] is called **“the holy of the Lord,”** regarding which it states **“and the holy of the Lord honorable.”**

**81. “He began and said, etc.” He began** his discourse **and said: “My Sabbaths** [ et Shabbetotai ]**”** (Leviticus 19:30). ** Et comes to include the Shabbat boundary, which is two thousand cubits in each direction. For this reason** the verse **added** the word ** et ,** alef - tav **. Shabbetotai ,** in the plural, **is the higher Shabbat and the lower Shabbat, which are two, incorporated together and sealed together.**

Explanation: **“ Et comes to include etc.”** Although it is stated: “Let no man go out of his place on the seventh day” (Exodus 16:29), by means of the word ** et ** the Torah added two thousand cubits in each direction, from beyond one’s place. ** Et ** is the mystical meaning of the Malkhut from whose fusion the brains of Abba and Imma emerged, which shine on Shabbat in addition to the illumination of the [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba . The Abba and Imma are the mystical meaning of two thousand. thus states **“for this reason, it added et ,”** as ** et ** thereby comes to include.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“ Shabbetotai is the higher Shabbat and the lower Shabbat.”** The higher Shabbat is Tevuna , while the lower Sabbath is Malkhut , the Nukba of Ze’er Anpin , which are called ** Mi ** and ** Ma ** (see section 8, above), or **“the higher world”** and **“the lower world”;** see there. They are **“incorporated together”** because on Shabbat [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba ascend and enclothe Abba and Imma. Thus, Tevuna and Malkhut are **incorporated** in each other **together** because the lower [entity] that ascends to the higher [entity] becomes like [the higher entity]. They are **“sealed together”** because despite this [incorporation], the Malkhut still does not become actual Tevuna without any distinction between them. This is because these brains of Tevuna are received by Malkhut only above, in the place of Tevuna , whereas in the actual place of Malkhut , below, [ Malkhut ] does not have these brains. In that sense, the Malkhut is still considered sealed [off from the brains]. He adds that Tevuna also suffers from the sealed state of Malkhut , for since their brains are **incorporated together**, they are therefore also **sealed together**. It follows that although Tevuna by itself is not sealed at all – as now on Shabbat [ Tevuna ] is a unified partzuf with Imma Ila’ah – nevertheless, since the brains [of Tevuna ] illuminate in one incorporation with the brains of the Malkhut , the sealing of Malkhut is therefore also detectable in the brains of Tevuna .

**82. “Another Shabbat was left, etc.” Another Shabbat was left, which was not mentioned, and she was ashamed. She said before Him: “Master of the Universe, since the day You made me, I have been called Shabbat, and there is no day without a night.” He said to her: “My daughter, you are Shabbat and I called you Shabbat. However, I am hereby crowning you with the highest crown.” He issued a declaration, saying: “Fear My sanctuary.” This is the Shabbat of Shabbat eve, which is fear and in which fear resides. Who is she?** He answers: **That which the Holy One, blessed be He, incorporated together and said, “I am the Lord**,” as “I” is the mystical meaning of Malkhut , which is the mystical meaning of Shabbat eve, [and] “the Lord” is Ze’er Anpin , and in the words **“I am the Lord”** they were incorporated together**. And I heard from my father that he said this and inferred** that the word ** et comes to include the Shabbat boundary. Shabbetotai ,** in the plural, **is the circle and square within it, which are two**, that is, two Shabbatot**. Corresponding to these two, there are two sanctities that we should mention: One is, “And** [the heaven and the earth] **were finished** [ Ve-yekhulu ]**”** (Genesis 2:1), **and** [the other] **one is Kiddush.** [The passage of] **“And they were finished” consists of thirty-five words, and in the Kiddush that we sanctify there are thirty-five words. Together, these all amount to the seventy names, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Assembly of Israel are crowned.**

**83. “And because this circle and square, etc.” And because this circle and square are “My Sabbaths” they are both incorporated in “keep** [ shamor ]**,” as it is stated: “Keep** My Sabbaths**”** (Leviticus 19:30)**. However, the higher Shabbat is not incorporated in “keep” but in “remember** [ zakhor ]**,” since the supernal king,** which is Bina , **was completed in “remember.” For this reason, the Bina is called a “king who has peace,” as his peace is “remember.” Therefore, there is no dispute above.**

Explanation: **“Another Shabbat was left, etc.”** This is the mystical meaning of the Malkhut of Malkhut , which is called “the middle point.” [This aspect of Malkhut ] does not receive brains even during the day of Shabbat, as [this aspect] itself is the mystical meaning of the manula (lock), and all the brains come only in the mystical meaning of the miftaḥa (key), which is Yesod of Malkhut (as stated in section 42, above). Since [the Malkhut of Malkhut ] did not receive brains, it was in a state of shame.

This is the meaning of the statement: **“Another Shabbat was left, which was not mentioned.”** This is the middle point that was not mentioned, which did not receive brains **and was ashamed. “She said before Him etc.” –** she claimed: **“Since the day You made me,”** that is, at the beginning of my emanation in the world of Adam Kadmon , **“I have been called Shabbat.”** All the brains were bestowed through me, as there was no other Malkhut in [the level of] Adam Kadmon , but merely the middle point, and it was diminished only during the second constriction, in the world of Atzilut .

She further contended: **“And there is no day without a night.”** This is a most wondrous mystical insight, as she argued that even on the first day it is stated: “And there was evening and there was morning, one day” (Genesis 1:5), [indicating] that the unity is revealed over day and night together. If so, why wasn’t night mentioned on the Shabbat of creation, as “night” is not written on the seventh day of the act of creation. **“He said to her...”** that is, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to her: **“You are Shabbat”** for the future, in the seventh millennium, on the day that is all Shabbat, **“and I called you Shabbat,”** that is, from the day I made you in the world of Adam Kadmon , as stated.

**“However, I am hereby crowning you etc.”** In other words, the Holy One, blessed be He, raised her up, so that she would serve in the first three of the partzufim (as stated in section 41, above). She was established as Malkhut of Abba and Imma Ila’in , in the mystical meaning of “unknown air; see there. Abba and Imma Ila’in are called “the holy of holies,” and thus she too is in the mystical meaning of the supernal holiness.

**“He issued a declaration, saying: ‘Fear My sanctuary. ’”** Through the establishing [of Malkhut ] in the Abba and Imma Ila’in , [this Malkhut ] is in the mystical meaning of a sanctuary, which is the mystical meaning of: “Fear My sanctuaries.” Thus, the Malkhut has now earned a supernal crown, more than it had in the world of Adam Kadmon . [In the world of Adam Kadmon , the Malkhut was serving at the place of the bottom end of the sefirot , in [the usual] place [of Malkhut ], whereas now [ Malkhut ] has risen to serve in the place of the first three [ sefirot , in Abba and Imma Ila’in , who are called “holy of holies.” He accordingly states: **“I am hereby crowning you with the highest crown.”**

[The Zohar ] continues: **“This is the Shabbat of Shabbat eve, which is fear etc.”** The Malkhut is called **“fear,”** as the constriction was performed upon Malkhut , so that it should not receive according to its measure. [ Malkhut ] does not use the direct light [that flows] from above downward for itself, but only the returning light, because [ Malkhut ] is established with a partition, with startling and fright, so that the light will not pass from the partition downward (as stated in section 56, above, s. v. Ve-kulhu ; see there). Now, upon the ascent [of Malkhut ] to the supernal holiness of [ Abba and Imma Ila’in ], a supernal **“fear resides”** in [ Malkhut ], since the supernal Havaya of Abba and Imma then resides in [ Malkhut ]. This is the mystical meaning the Shabbat eve that was now established, in accordance with her claim, **“there is no day without a night,”** and **“this is the Shabbat of Shabbat eve.”** The attribute of night is also incorporated in the day of Shabbat. He then asks: **“What is he”;** what is the fear that resides in it? **“That which the Holy One, blessed be He, incorporated together and said, ‘I am the Lord’,”** since the supernal Havaya of Abba and Imma is incorporated in [ Malkhut ], and [the Torah] stated, “I am the Lord.” In order to clarify this, he cites a teaching that he heard from his father.

The explanation of these things is that the image of the circle conveys that the light shines there equally in all places, and there is no aspect of judgment there at all, on account of which any change should occur in the measure of illumination. The image of the square conveys that there is an aspect of judgment there, because of which it is possible to differentiate between right and left, or east and west. This is why the head is regarded as in the shape of a circle, relative to the body, which is a square. For in the first three [ sefirot ], which is the head, there are no judgments, whereas there are judgments in the body, as generally there is right and left in the body, front and back.

Now, you already know the mystical meaning of Shabbat, that [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba ascend and enclothe Abba and Imma, forming] the aspect of **“the higher Shabbat and the lower Shabbat are incorporated together,”** as stated above. The higher Shabbat, which is Abba and Imma , is considered the aspect of **“circle,”** while the lower Shabbat, which is [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , the aspect of the body, is considered the aspect of **“square.”** Accordingly, on Shabbat the [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba of the square ascend and are incorporated in the Abba and Imma , which are the aspect of circle. He thus states: **“ Shabbetotai is the circle and square within it, which are two.”** This is why the verse states **“My Sabbaths** [ Shabbetotai ],” in order to include two Shabbatot: The higher Shabbat, which is a **“circle,”** and the **“square”** inside it, which is the lower Shabbat that ascended and was incorporated within it.

Now, the brains of Ḥokhma are called **“seventy names,”** or “seventy crowns,” as ayin [70] alludes to Ḥokhma . Since these brains are revealed only through the ascent of the lower Shabbat to the higher one, the brains are thus divided between the pair of them: Half of them to the higher Shabbat and half of them to the lower Shabbat. Consequently, “[the passage of] **‘and they were finished’ consists of thirty-five words,”** which are half of the brains in the higher Shabbat, while Kiddush itself contains thirty-five words, alluding to the half of the brains that are in the lower Shabbat. These are the brains that **“the Assembly of Israel,”** which is the Malkhut that is called Shabbat, is **“crowned.”**

[The Zohar ] continues: **“And because this circle and square etc.”** In other words, since the circle and the square are together incorporated in **“My Sabbaths,”** it follows that the brains of the circle are also in the aspect of **“keep,”** like the square, even though “keep” indicates judgment and a boundary from which one should keep his distance. In the higher Shabbat, which is a circle, there is no judgment (as stated below). Nevertheless, due to its mingling together with the Shabbat of a square, the aspect of **“keep”** also applies to the circle.

**“However, the higher Shabbat is not incorporated in ‘keep. ’”** The higher Shabbat itself is incorporated in **“remember”** rather than **“keep,”** since the supernal king was completed in “remember,” and contains no expression of judgment at all, that it should be suitable to say **“keep”** about him, as “keep” applies only to the Nukba . Nevertheless, with respect to the incorporation of the higher Shabbat in the lower Shabbat, **“keep”** applies to both of them together, although not to the higher Shabbat by itself.

**“As his peace is ‘remember. ’ Therefore, there is no dispute above. ’”** The supernal king is the mystical meaning of the Bina that was completed with [the letter] yod , which is the mystical meaning of the male garments (as stated in section 17 above; see there). This indicates that there is no aspect of **dispute** there at all, that is, it is without any judgments, for this is why [this Shabbat] is called “a circle” (as explained above). However, the lower Shabbat, which is the mystical meaning of Ma , was completed with [the letter] heh , and therefore there is [the aspect of] dispute in [this lower Shabbat], that is, right and left. For this reason, it is called a “square.”

**84. “For there are two ‘peaces, ’ etc.” For there are two “peaces” below. One is Jacob,** which is Tiferet , **and** [the other] **one is Joseph**, which is Yesod **. This is why** “peace” **is written twice: “Peace, peace, to he who is far off and to he who is near”** (Isaiah 57:19)**. “To he who is far” is Jacob; “and to he who is near” is Joseph. “To he who is far,” as it is stated: “From afar the Lord appeared to me”** (Jeremiah 31:2)**, and likewise: “And his sister stood afar off”** (Exodus 2:4)**. “To he who is near** [ ve-lakarov ]**,” as it is stated: “New ones, who came up recently** [ mi-karov ]**”** (Deuteronomy 32:17)**.**

Explanation: **“For there are two ‘peaces’ below, etc.”** “Below” means in [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , which contain the aspect of **Jacob,** which is Tiferet , and also the aspect of **Joseph,** which is Yesod . This alludes to the two aspects of fusion that are in [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , since **“peace”** is the mystical meaning of a [fusion through collision]. There is the aspect of higher fusion, to drawing forth the height of Ḥokhma , and there is a lower fusion, for drawing forth [the light of giving]. The higher one is the mystical meaning of **Jacob** and the lower one is the mystical meaning of **Joseph**.

As explained earlier (section 14, fourth paragraph), the seven lower [ sefirot ] cannot receive the height of Ḥokhma without [the light of giving], and therefore the height of Ḥokhma in [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba is considered to be far from them, since they can receive [the height of Ḥokhma ] only by enclothing it in [the light of giving]. This is the mystical meaning of: **“From afar the Lord appeared to me,”** since the height of Ḥokhma is far from him and he needs to enclothe [it] in order to receive it.

Therefore, Jacob’s aspect of **peace** is called **“far,”** while the lower fusion, which is the **peace** of Joseph, is called **“near,”** for it is received without clothing [of the light of giving]. Moreover, because of the height of [the light of giving in the aspect of Joseph], it can receive [the light of] Ḥokhma as well (as stated in section 14). This is the mystical meaning of the verse: **“Peace, peace, to he who is far off and to he who is near,”** [referring to] two “peaces,” of **Jacob and Joseph,** which always operate in the fusion of maturity of [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba . There is a dispute in these **“two peaces”** that are in [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , which are considered the mystical meaning of a **square,** and [ Ze’er Anpin and Nukba ] end in [the letter] heh , which is the mystical meaning of female. This is not the case for the supernal king, the mystical meaning of Bina ; [this structure] ends in [the letter] yod , the mystical meaning of male, and there is no dispute in [this structure]. Even the dynamic of **far and near** does not apply in Bina itself, as [ Bina ] is of the aspect of the first three [ sefirot ], and the first three can receive Ḥokhma **“in the near,”** that is, they do not need to enclothe [the light of Ḥokhma ] in [the light of giving] at all, and they receive Ḥokhma without [the light of giving]. This is alluded to above, that **“the supernal king”** is the “king who has peace” (section 83), and [the supernal king] does not contain **two “peaces,”** the way [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba [do].

**85. “‘From afar, ’ this is the uppermost point etc.” “From afar”** (Jeremiah 31:2)**, this is the uppermost point that stands in His sanctuary. With regard to this, it is written “you shall keep”** (Leviticus 19:30)**,** that is, **it is included in “keep.” “And you shall fear My sanctuary”** (Leviticus 19:30) **is the point that is positioned in the middle, which should be feared most of all, as its punishment is death, and this is** [the meaning of] **that which is stated: “Everyone who profanes it shall surely be put to death”** (Exodus 31:14)**. Who is he “who profanes it”?
