This is why it states: **“‘And slew him with his own spear,” on account of that sin that he struck the rock with that staff, he died.”** Had [Moses] been careful to use [the staff] only at the ** tzor ** and not at the ** sela ** [rock], the aspect of Sag would not have been nullified together with the Ban and he would not have **died** but would have immediately ascended to the aspect of Sag . Accordingly, he **“did not enter the holy land,”** because the Land of Israel is the mystical meaning of the ascent of the Ban to the Sag . This is why it is called “**the holy land,”** because the brains of Bina , which then illuminate in it, are called **“holiness.”** Before the completion of the rectification, when there are ascents and descents, there are therefore destructions and exiles. However, at the completion of the rectification, the Ban will remain in the Sag for all eternity, which is the mystical meaning of the Land of Israel, as explained, and there will never be any further exile.

**103. “He was most honorable of the thirty, etc.” “He was most honorable of the thirty”** (see II Samuel 23:19, 23)**. These are the upper thirty years, from which he would take and extend below. From them he would take and draw near, “but did not come to the three”** (II Samuel 23:19)**.** Rather, **they would come to him and give him willingly, but he did not come to them.**

Explanation: The first three [ sefirot ], which are Ḥokhma , Bina , and Da’at , are called **“the thirty,”** that is, three sefirot , each of which is comprised of ten [ sefirot ], and which are the entirety of the brains that illuminate during the six thousand years. The soul of **Benayahu,** which comes from the great fusion of the Atik Yomin , collects all the fusions of the six thousand years, in the mystical meaning of **“who had done many deeds, the God gatherer,”** into a single height, which is Benayahu Ben Yehoyada, as stated. Thus, he receives and is honored by all those supernal thirty years.

This is the meaning of **“from which he would take and extend below.”** He would take from the brains of **thirty** years, which extend to his soul **below**, at the bottom of them all. **“From them he would take and draw near,”** since his whole height is only from what he took and gathered from their fusions, which came one after another, as explained previously. Despite [his acquiring of this height], **“‘but did not come to the three” – they would come to him and give him willingly, but he did not come to them.”** For although they gave him all of his sublime quality **willingly,** he still could not come to them afterward and receive more from them. The reason is as stated, that due to the nullification of the partition of Ban , the partition of Sag was nullified as well, and he was left without a partition. Therefore, he could not come to them to raise feminine waters and receive more [brains] from them.

**104. “Even though he was still not included, etc.” Even though he was still not included in their number and calculation, it is nevertheless written: “And David set him over his guard”** (II Samuel 23:23), [meaning] **that he was never parted from the tablet of his heart,** for **they will never be separated. David set his heart upon him, but he did not set his heart upon David. This is because the praises, songs, and mercies that the moon performs toward the sun thereby pull toward her, so that his dwelling is with her. This is** [the meaning of]**: “And David set him over his guard.”**

Explanation: David is the aspect of Malkhut , the fourth leg of the first three [ sefirot ]. The meaning is that although [Benayahu] could not come to the supernal thirty years, which are the first three [ sefirot ], nevertheless “David set him over his guard,” meaning that [Benayahu] clung to [David] and **never** moved from the tablet of his heart. The reason is that aspect of wholeness within Malkhut was revealed through [David], since he is from the great fusion of the Atik Yomin , which detaches all the kelippot from the name Ban , in the mystical meaning of the verse: “He will eliminate death forever” (Isaiah 25:8, as stated in section 94, above, third paragraph; see there).

[The Zohar ] continues: **“David set his heart upon him,”** as stated above, **“that he was never parted from the tablet of his heart,”** since [David’s] wholeness was within him. However, **Benayahu Ben Yehoyada** did not set his heart **upon David,** because David is the fourth leg of the first three [ sefirot ]. Accordingly, just as [Benayahu] cannot receive from the first three [ sefirot ], he could not receive **from David**, and therefore he did not set his heart upon him.

**“Praises, songs** etc.” By means of the feminine waters, which the Malkhut – called the **moon** – raises to Ze’er Anpin ], called the **sun**, through the praises, songs, and mercies, [the Malkhut ] draws to itself the illumination of the soul of Benayahu Ben Yehoyada, which is the final wholeness [of Malkhut ] (as stated), **“so that his dwelling is with her,”** that he will cleave to [the Malkhut ] forever.

**105. Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Abba fell down before him**, on their faces**. While doing so, they could not see him. They stood up and looked to all sides, but they did not see him. They sat and wept, and could not speak to one another. Afterwards, Rabbi Abba said: “This must be what we learned, that on whatever path way the righteous walk and there are words of Torah among them, the righteous from that world come** to reveal words of Torah **to them. This must be Rav Hamnuna Saba who came to us from that world, to reveal these matters to us, but before we were able to recognize him, he went away and disappeared from us. They arose and wished to drive the donkeys, but** the donkeys **would not go. They** again **wanted to drive them, but they** [still] **would not go. They grew afraid and left the donkeys, and to this day, they call that place “the place of the donkeys.”**

Explanation: They could not bear that great light that appeared to them upon the revelation of these secrets, and they bowed down before him. This is the meaning of **“Rabbi Elazar** [and Rabbi Abba] **fell down** etc.”

[The Zohar ] continues: **“While doing so, they could not see him.”** After they merited to receive his great, sublime level from him, he immediately vanished from them, and they could no longer find and perceive him. Therefore, **“they sat and wept, and could not speak to one another.”** They were so upset that they sat down and wept until they could no longer converse with each other.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“This must be Rav Hamnuna Saba...**” for they now recognized his level, that he was **Rav Hamnuna Saba** himself, not merely the son of Rav Hamnuna Saba, as they had previously assumed (see section 90, above). **“They arose and wished to drive the donkeys**…**and left the donkeys” –** for the donkeys are the mystical meaning of the abilities that the soul of Rav Hamnuna Saba had given them, to be able to raise feminine waters in order to attain the levels of ḥaya and yeḥida , which they attained through him.

This is the mystical meaning of his placing them on the donkeys and walking before them to illuminate the path of the righteous for them (as stated in section 85, above, seventh paragraph). Now, after he completed his task and vanished from them, they wanted to climb up and ride his donkeys once again, that is, they wished to raise feminine waters afresh, in order to perceive him a second time. However, **“they wished to drive the donkeys, but they would not go,”** for now they were no longer able to receive from them the strength to raise feminine waters. They therefore became afraid and left the donkeys in that place where Rav Hamnuna Saba had disappeared from them. They labeled that place “the place of the donkeys,” that is, they named it after what occurred there, that they were no longer able to use them.

**106. “Rabbi Elazar began, etc.” Rabbi Elazar began** his discourse **by saying: “How great is Your goodness You have in store for those who fear You etc.”** (Psalms 31:20)**. How** [great] **is the supernal, precious good that the Holy One, blessed be He, will perform for people, for those lofty righteous ones who fear sin, who engage in the Torah, when they come to that world. It does not write “Your goodness,” but “great is Your goodness.” What is this? This is: “They shall utter the fame of Your great goodness”** (Psalms 145:7)**, and this is the life of delight that extends from the next world to the one who lives forever. It is called “the fame of Your great goodness,” and it is certainly “the great goodness toward the house of Israel”** (Isaiah 63:7)**.**

Explanation: The word rav [“great”] invariably denotes greatness. Since the verse here emphasizes **“great is Your goodness,”** and not simply **“Your goodness,”** it is referring to **“the life of delight,”** that is, the brains of the first three [ sefirot ]. The essence of the partzuf , and its lifeforce, is the brains of the [level of the] six extremities, which is received from the fusion of Abba and Imma (father and mother) in order to sustain the worlds. However, there are also additional levels of brains [beyond this basic level], which delight the living. These are the brains of the first three [ sefirot ] and they are called **“great goodness”** and **“a life of delight.”**

[The Zohar ] continues: **“That extends from the next world to the one who lives forever.”** The brains of the first three [ sefirot ], which are Ḥokhma , are drawn from Bina , which is called “the next world,” and the [first three] are enclothed in the precious garment of [the light of giving], which comes from the fusion of the Yesodot , called **“the one who lives forever.”** From there, the brains reach the righteous **“who fear sin.”**

**107. “Furthermore, “How great, etc.” Furthermore,** we can interpret **“How** [ ma ] **great is Your goodness”** [as teaching] that **here the secret of the Ḥokhma is engraved, and all the secrets are incorporated here.** For the meaning of ** ma is as we learned** (in section 19, above)**. “Great” is a great and strong tree,** which is Ze’er Anpin , **since there is a smaller tree than him**, that is, the Malkhut **. This** Ze’er Anpin **is great and he brings him into the height of the firmaments.**

Explanation: In addition to [the previous] interpretation of the verse as referring to the attainment of the brains of the first three [ sefirot ], it can also be understood as recording the inner [aspects] of the Ḥokhma , and “all the secrets are incorporated” into this verse. **“The secret of the Ḥokhma ”** means the fusion of the Atik ; **“and all the secrets”** refers to the completion of the total rectification.

**“ Ma is as we learned; ‘great’ is a great and strong tree.”** Ma is the lower world, as stated earlier (section 8). **“Great”** means **a great and strong tree,** that is, Ze’er Anpin at the time of its enclothing of the partzuf of Ab , at which time [ Ze’er Anpin ] is called **“a great tree,”** as a result of the [access to] Ḥokhma , and [ Ze’er Anpin ] is called **“strong”** with regard to itself. However, when Ze’er Anpin is in its own place, it is termed merely **“a tree.”** This is the meaning of **“since there is a smaller tree than him,”** which is the Malkhut ,” which is also called “a tree.” **“This is great” –** for when [ Ze’er Anpin ] enclothes the level of Ab , [ Ze’er Anpin ] is called **“great.” “And he brings him into the height of the firmaments”** – the Ab brings the Ze’er Anpin to **“the height of the firmaments.”** The height of Ab reaches until the Keter , which is called **“the height of the firmaments,”** since the Ab enclothes over the partzuf of Keter . Thus, Ab raises the Ze’er Anpin to **“the height of the firmaments.”**

**108. “‘Your goodness’ is the light, etc.” “Your goodness” is the light that was created on the first day** of the act of creation. **“You have in store for those who fear You,”** that is, **for He concealed it on behalf of the righteous for that world. “Which You have created** [ pa’alta ]**” is the upper Garden of Eden, as it is stated: “The place You fashioned** [ pa’alta ] **for Your dwelling, Lord”** (Exodus 15:17). **This is** [the meaning of]: **“Which You have created for those taking refuge in You”** (Psalms 31:20).

Explanation: The light that was created on the first day is the light through which Adam the first [man] gazed from one end of the world to the other. This is the mystical meaning of the five times “light” is mentioned on the first day of the act of creation. **“On behalf of the righteous for that world,”** that is, in the World-to-Come, since that light was concealed in the foundations, which are the righteous [ tzaddik ] and justice [ tzedek ] of the Abba and Imma (father and mother), called the World-to-Come. Those tzaddik and tzedek are called “those who fear You,” [named] after the power of concealment that is within them. This light is received by the righteous from them.

**“‘Which You have created** [ pa’alta ]’ **is the upper Garden of Eden,”** since it is previously written: “**You have in store,”** which means that the brains come in a precious garment of tzaddik and tzedek , in concealment, covered by those garments. And here it is written, **“which You have created,”** meaning an open act, without the aforementioned cover. [The Zohar ] cites a proof from the verse: **“The place You fashioned** [ pa’alta ] **for Your dwelling, Lord,”** that is, a complete and open act.

[The Zohar ] expounds that [the phrase] **“which You have created”** refers to the upper **Garden of Eden,** which is actuated and excluded from the category of those brains mentioned previously in the verse, which are in effect throughout the whole 6, 000 years. The verse should thus be read as follows: **“How great is the goodness You have in store for those who fear You,”** which are the brains of the entire 6, 000 years, for **“You have created”** all of these by means of the great fusion of the Atik Yomin . **“For those taking refuge in You,”** since the upper Garden of Eden is actuated and emerges from these brains, [and the upper Garden of Eden is] where the completely righteous stay, those who take refuge in Him, that is, souls such as Benayahu Ben Yehoyada. These merit to receive from the fusion of the [ Atik Yomin ], which is gathered from all those brains of the 6, 000 years, as stated.

Know that the resting place of the souls is called **“the Garden of Eden.”** There is the earthly Garden of Eden, which is also called “the lower Garden of Eden,” and which is of the aspect of six extremities. There is the upper Garden of Eden, which is the aspect of the first three [ sefirot ] of the Garden of Eden. All the souls stay only in the lower Garden of Eden. However, on New Moons and on Shabbatot they ascend to the upper Garden of Eden, after which they return to their place. But there are a select few whose place is in the upper Garden of Eden, regarding which Rabbi Shimon said: “I have seen the men of ascent, that they are few.”

**109. “In front of people” “In front of people”** (Psalms 31:20). **This is the lower Garden of Eden, where all the righteous stand in a spirit enclothed in a precious garment, in the same way and form as they were in this world. This is** [the meaning of the phrase] **“in front of people,”** that is, **in the same form of people in this world. They stand there and fly in the air** from there **and ascend to the academy of the firmament in that Garden of Eden of above. They fly there and bathe in the dew of rivers of pure persimmon, and descend and stay below,** in the lower Garden of Eden.

Explanation: The main difference between the first three [ sefirot ] and the seven lower [ sefirot ], both in the partzufim and the [individual] souls is that the [level of the] first three [ sefirot ] can receive the light of Ḥokhma as it is, and they do not need the Ḥokhma to be enclothed for them in a garment of the light of giving. This is not the case for the partzufim of the six extremities, and likewise the souls that are born from [ Ze’er Anpin ] and Nukba , which are the essence of [the level of] six extremities – these [souls] can receive the light of Ḥokhma only when it is enclothed in the light of giving.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“This is the lower Garden of Eden, where all the righteous stand in a spirit enclothed in a precious garment, in the same way and form as they were in this world.”** The spirits of all the righteous in the lower Garden of Eden are enclothed in a precious garment of the light of giving, like the souls of people in this world. By means of this **“precious garment,”** called **“air,”** they can ascend to the upper Garden of Eden and receive the light of Ḥokhma from there, and subsequently return to their place in the lower Garden of Eden.

**“They stand there”** means that their main, fixed place is in the lower Garden of Eden. **“And fly in the air and ascend to the academy of the firmament in that Garden of Eden of above.”** Through the strength of this **“air,”** which is the [enclothing garment of the] light of giving, they fly and ascend to the upper Garden of Eden to receive Ḥokhma . **“They fly there and bathe in the dew of rivers of pure persimmon,”** since the light of Ḥokhma that they receive there, in the Garden of Eden, is called “**thirteen rivers of pure persimmon,”** for the Ḥokhma is called **“oil,”** and the number **thirteen** alludes to the Ḥokhma of the thirty-two paths (as stated above, in Marot HaSulam , s. v., Ve’im ).

They then **“descend and stay below,”** because they cannot remain there. Immediately after receiving the Ḥokhma within their **precious garment,** they descend from the upper Garden of Eden to their place, to the lower Garden of Eden. Since they need to receive the Ḥokhma within the garment [formed of the light of giving], like the souls of people in this world, the verse calls them as well, “in front of people.” [This is] because they have the same form as people in this world, since [the people of this world] also require the clothing of [the light of giving] like [these souls].

**110. “Sometimes, they appear etc.” Sometimes,** these righteous ones **appear in front of people, to make miracles for them, like the upper angels, such as we saw now, the light of the supernal illumination. But we did not merit to observe and further know the secrets of the wisdom.**

Explanation: This is referring to the souls of the select few in the upper Garden of Eden. Their quality is so lofty that even the souls in the lower Garden of Eden who ascend to them on the New Moons and on Shabbatot cannot remain there, but promptly descend to their places. Nevertheless, they **“sometimes appear in front of people,”** descending from the upper Garden of Eden to this world and appear to people like upper angels that occasionally descend to this world. This is [the meaning of the phrase]: **“Such as we saw now, the light of the supernal illumination,”** that is, just as he now saw the light of the supernal illumination, that is, of Rav Hamnuna Saba, who descended to them from the loftiness of his level, from the upper Garden of Eden, and was revealed to them in this world.
The verse **“in front of people”** is thus expounded in two ways:

1. In reference to the souls in the lower Garden of Eden, that they have **“the form of people.”** He fashioned for them the lofty lights in the upper Garden of Eden so that they could receive from there by ascending on the New Moons and on Shabbatot, since then they merit to greet the souls in the upper Garden of Eden before descending once again back to their places.
2. “In front of people” literally, in this world, that is, these souls in the upper Garden of Eden sometimes descend to this world like the celestial angels and appear to the righteous.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“But we did not merit to observe and further know the secrets of the wisdom.”** The complaint is that he promptly disappeared from them, and from that time onward, they have not merited to attain any more **secrets of the Torah.**

**111. “Rabbi Abba opened etc.” Rabbi Abba opened** [his discourse] **and said: “And Manoah said to his wife: We shall surely die, because we have seen God”** (Judges 13:22). **Even though Manoah did not understand his actions,** as it is written, “For Manoah did not know that he was an angel of the Lord” (Judges 13:16), nevertheless, **he said: Since it is stated: “For man shall not see Me and live”** (Exodus 33:20), **and we have certainly seen, therefore “we will surely die.” Now, we saw and merited this light that was walking with us, and** yet **we still exist in the world. For the Holy One, blessed be He, sent it to us, to inform us the secrets of the wisdom that it revealed. Happy is our portion.**

Explanation: When the angel of the Lord appeared to Manoah, his comprehension [of the angel] was incomplete, for the angel did not wish to tell him his name, as it is stated: “Why do you ask for my name, seeing it is hidden?” (Judges 13:18). Despite this [incompleteness], he feared the verse: **“For man shall not see Me and live.”** But we merited the complete comprehension, since we knew his name, which is **Rav Hamnuna Saba,** and [yet] we are alive and exist in this world. From here you can understand that greeting the level of Rav Hamnuna Saba is an expression of: “Show me, I pray, Your glory” (Exodus 33:19), which Moses asked from the Lord, in response to which the Lord informed him: “You cannot see My face, for man shall not see Me and live.” It follows that their comprehension was greater than that of Moses, and with regard to this the Sages stated: “It is a prophet that did not arise like Moses [see Deuteronomy 34:10], but a Sage did arise [who was equal to him]” (end of Yalkut Reuveini ), and similarly [their statement that] “a Sage is preferable to a prophet” ( Bava Batra 12a).
